subject: Urgent — GammaApps: sudden TPS suppression & p99 regressions post-quant rollout
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@gammaapps.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, support@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production — sudden throughput drop, p99 spike

Hey team,

We started seeing a sharp drop in tokens/sec for our Hosted API requests starting ~03:20 PDT this morning. p95 is up ~2.1s (baseline ~0.6s) and p99 is spiking above 3s for our typical 1k-token requests. Throughput (tokens/sec) across our key routes is down ~55%. This aligns with the time the platform notes a quantization rollout to q4_2 for performance testing.

Attached are metric screenshots and a short dtrace log. This is impacting our live chat SLA — can someone take a look now? We need a remediation plan and ETA.

- Samira
GammaApps — Head of Platform

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production — sudden throughput drop, p99 spike

Preliminary triage notes (fast):
- Confirmed: q4_2 quantization profile was promoted at 03:05 PDT to a subset of hosted-api nodes as part of a cross-tenant perf test. GammaApps' traffic was routed to a canary pool that received the change.
- Observed behavior: kernel selector is choosing a different attention/kernel path for 1k-token sequences under q4_2; that path has higher memory move overhead and shows much lower tokens/sec in our microbenchmarks (reproducer attached).
- NVLink / scheduler pressure on those hosts increased around the same time (dtrace shows NVLink stalls correlating with the slower kernel).

Immediate recommendation:
1) Roll back GammaApps' nodes to q8_0 (previous default) and pin kernel selector to 'legacy-fast' for the tenant.
2) Do a 10% canary rollback to validate improvement, then 100% after 10m if metrics look good.
3) Keep a tracing session and token-rate sampling active for 1 hour post-rollback.

I can execute steps 1–2. Attaching reproducer: reproducer-q4_2.tar.gz (microbench + config).

- Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production — sudden throughput drop, p99 spike

Action log:
- 10:12 PDT: Opened maintenance window for GammaApps tenant in us-west-2.
- 10:18 PDT: Pinned kernel selector to 'legacy-fast' on the affected node pool and rolled back quant profile to q8_0 for GammaApps.
- 10:22 PDT: Canary to 10% traffic for 3 nodes. Observed immediate improvement: tokens/sec +48% on canary, p95 back within baseline range (~0.65s), p99 trending down.
- 10:25 PDT: Promoted rollback to 100% for GammaApps; monitoring.

Attached: gamma_prod_metrics_20270515.png (post-rollback snapshot).

Notes / follow-ups:
- We'll keep the kernel selector pin for 48 hours for GammaApps while Rishi's team prepares a fix to the q4_2 compatibility check.
- Need to audit the rollout gating: canary pool selection should have excluded high-seq customers by default.

- Markus
Head of SRE
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@gammaapps.com>, ops@gammaapps.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production — rapid update and remediation

Samira — quick update from our side: we identified the root cause as a quant profile (q4_2) interaction with the kernel selector that can pick a slower kernel path for long-sequence requests. Markus rolled back GammaApps' nodes to the prior quant profile (q8_0) and pinned the kernel selector; we validated recovery in canary and then at 100%. Your p95/p99 and tokens/sec are back to baseline as of 10:25 PDT.

Immediate next steps:
- Rishi's team will prepare a patch to the q4_2 compatibility checks and adjust the kernel selector heuristic (ETA 48–72 hours).
- We'll keep the pin for 48 hours and run an extended smoke test with GammaApps traffic.
- As a goodwill gesture for the incident window (03:20–10:25 PDT) we propose a 15% service credit on billable Hosted API tokens for the impacted interval; Laura will follow up with the formal credit note.

Would you like to schedule a 30-min post-incident call Monday to walk the mitigation and timeline? Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the flag and your patience.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
